answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity a capital-time escrow: each slot locks a minimum bond the ledger commits, so one coin cannot back two slots, and influence is capped at its zenith of one vote per slot. Splitting a fortune only subdivides it; N clones need N separate bonds locked over the same horizon, so extra identities buy no multiplier, only more docked at the same wharf of committed capital. The scarce resource is basalt-solid locked coin, non-shareable by double-spend protection. Linear cost deters cheap minting, not a rich funder; it trusts the ledger's escrow.
